summary: Anne M. Blackburn works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago (1991) and held posts at Cornell University (Assistant Professor of Religion, ~2001–2021) and Harvard University (Professor, ~2021).

Anne MacDonald specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied at the University of British Columbia (attested 1988) and under Shotaro Iida, among others. Her posts include the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (Professor, 2010).

Anne Nishimura Morse specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, Taka Yanagisawa, and Yutaka Hirata. Her appointments include Smith College (1988–1989) and visiting scholar posts at Tokyo, Nara, and Kyoto national institutions.

Anne Ruth Hansen works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history. She studied under Charles Hallisey. Her career includes posts at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2007) and the University of Wisconsin–Madison (Associate Professor attested 2012; Professor attested 2026).

Anne-Marie Blondeau is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under Marcelle Lalou, Rolf Alfred Stein, Dagpo Rinpoche, Yonten Gyatso, and Geshe Ngawang Dakpa, and held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (attested 1982, 2003).

Anne-Marie Esnoul (1908–1996) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and the EPHE under Sylvain Lévi, Paul Masson-Oursel, and Nadine Stchoupak. She held posts at ICI (1941–1966) and EPHE (1966–1977).
Annegret Bollée (1937–2021) was a linguist. She pursued her studies at the University of Hamburg (~1957), Aix-Marseille University, and the University of Bonn (1969).

Annelies Kammenhuber (1922–1995) worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied under Ferdinand Sommer at Munich and Hamburg (Ph.D. 1950, PD ~1958–1960). She held professorships at the Pontifical Biblical Institute (1968) and Munich (1964–1987).

Annemarie Schimmel (1922–2003) studied at Berlin and Marburg under Hans Heinrich Schaeder and Friedrich Heiler. A scholar of religious studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology, she held professorships at Marburg, Ankara (1954–1967), Bonn, and Harvard (1967–1992).

Annemarie von Gabain (1901–1993) was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Berlin and studied at Peking University. She taught at Ankara University, Berlin (1939–1945), and Hamburg (1949–1966).

Annette Baier (1929–2012) was a philosopher. She studied at the University of Otago (~1948–1952) and Somerville College (PhD 1952). Her academic career included posts at Carnegie Mellon University (~1968–1973) and the University of Pittsburgh (~1973–1995).

Annette L. Heitmann specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1987–1989) and the University of Vienna (doctoral degree, 2002), studying under Christian Lindtner and David Seyfort Ruegg.

Annette Schmiedchen works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1989–1994) and her Habilitation at Halle-Wittenberg (~2001–2007), holding posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~2004), Humboldt University (~2011), and the International Association of Sanskrit Studies.

Annette Susannah Beveridge (1842–1929) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. She pursued her education at Bedford College, London, studying there from ~1858–1860 and 1862–1867.
Annie Barber Clarke (1861–1956) was an Indologist. She studied at Radcliffe College (1883–1886) under Charles Rockwell Lanman. She later held teaching posts at Parsons School and Miss Brown's School.

Annie Montaut is a linguist and Indologist. She studied at ENS, Paris Cité University, and Paris Nanterre under Nicole Balbir. She held academic posts at JNU (1981–1987), Paris Nanterre (1987–1990), and INALCO (1990–2014).

Anshul Agarwal works in computational studies and Indology. He completed a Bachelor of Engineering at Vivekanand Education Society's Institute of Technology in 2014 and held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur.

Antanas Poška (1903–1992) was a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Vytautas Magnus University (1926–1929), earned a B.A. from the University of Mumbai (1931–1933), and pursued doctoral studies at the University of Calcutta (~1933–1936).

Anthony C. Yu (1938–2015) was a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at Houghton University, Fuller Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. ~1963–1969), where he later served as a Distinguished Service Professor Emeritus (~2005–2015).

Anthony Cerulli specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees at Loyola University Chicago, Yale, and the University of Chicago (Ph.D. 2007). He held posts at Hobart and William Smith Colleges (2008–2016) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (2016–2021).
